title: The Car Driving Test: How It Works
whatItIs: The car test checks that a pupil can drive safely in different road and traffic conditions and shows knowledge of The Highway Code by the way they drive.
keyFacts: 4 parts: eyesight check, 'show me, tell me' questions, general driving (with independent driving) and reversing.
Around 35 minutes of driving. The regulations require at least 30 minutes on the road for a car test.
Independent driving lasts 20 to 35 minutes, following a sat nav or traffic signs. The examiner sets the sat nav.
The 'tell me' question comes before driving; the 'show me' question is asked while driving.
An emergency stop is carried out in 1 in every 7 car tests.
The test includes a normal stop, pulling out from behind a parked vehicle and a hill start.

items.title: Eyesight check
items.text: Read a number plate from 20 m (20.5 m, old-style plate). Fail and the test ends.

items.title: 'Tell me' question
items.text: Asked at the start, before the pupil drives.

items.title: General driving
items.text: No motorways. Includes independent driving and the 'show me' question.

items.title: Reversing
items.text: Parallel park, bay park, or pull up on the right and reverse about 2 car lengths.

a.label: Pupil's own car
points: Extra interior mirror and passenger head restraint for the examiner
L plates front and rear; taxed, MOT if needed, insured for a test

b.label: Hire car
points: Must be fitted with dual controls
Must meet all the other rules for test cars

onTheTest.question: A pupil wants to take the test in their own car. Which of these must the car have?
options: An extra interior rear-view mirror for the examiner
A dashcam that records inside the car
onTheTest.why: A test car must have an extra interior rear-view mirror for the examiner. Your own car does not need dual controls, and a space-saver spare must not be fitted.

onTheTest.question: During independent driving your pupil takes a wrong turning but drives safely. How does the examiner deal with this?
options: No fault; the examiner helps them back on the route
The independent section is ended and the test fails
onTheTest.why: The examiner will not give a fault for a wrong turning and will help the candidate back on route (GOV.UK; DT1 1.03).

traps: A pass in a semi-automatic car only lets you drive automatic and semi-automatic cars.
The candidate cannot use their own sat nav, self-parking or autopilot on the test.
Failed? The next test must be at least 10 working days away.
An extended test (after a ban) means around 65 minutes of driving.
